rows.stem:
To balance the following chemical equation the values of \(x\) and y should respectively be :

\(\mathrm{2NaOH} + x\,\mathrm{Al_2O_3} \longrightarrow \mathrm{y}\,\mathrm{NaAlO_2 + H_2O}\)
rows.solution:
Take \(x = 1\). One \(\mathrm{Al_2O_3}\) carries two aluminium atoms, so two \(\mathrm{NaAlO_2}\) are needed on the right, giving \(y = 2\).

\(\mathrm{2NaOH + Al_2O_3 \rightarrow 2NaAlO_2 + H_2O}\)

Check: Na 2 = 2; Al 2 = 2; H 2 = 2; O 2 + 3 = 5 on the left and 4 + 1 = 5 on the right.

So x and y are 1 and 2, which is option (B) 1, 2.

rows.stem: A solution turns the colour of turmeric to reddish brown. If the same solution is poured on universal indictor, its colour would change to –
rows.solution:
Turmeric turns reddish brown only in a basic solution, so the solution is a base, with a pH above 7. On universal indicator a basic solution shows blue, and the blue grows darker, towards violet, as the pH rises. CBSE keys blue on that reading.

A very strong base (pH around 13 to 14) actually turns universal indicator violet, so a student who chooses violet has a case: the question does not say how strong the base is. Blue is the expected answer for a base in general.

This is option (B) blue.

rows.stem: Given below are two columns, Column I shows enzymes secreted by the glands in the alimentary canal of human beings and Column II indicates the components of food on which enzymes act. Choose the options showing correct matching :

options.label: A
options.text: Column I (Enzymes): Pepsin; Column II (Component): Starch

options.label: B
options.text: Column I (Enzymes): Trypsin; Column II (Component): Proteins

options.label: C
options.text: Column I (Enzymes): Lipase; Column II (Component): Proteins

options.label: D
options.text: Column I (Enzymes): Amylase; Column II (Component): Emulsified fat

rows.solution:
Pepsin, secreted by the gastric glands of the stomach, acts on proteins, not starch. Trypsin, from the pancreas, digests proteins. Lipase acts on emulsified fats, not proteins, and amylase acts on starch, not fats.

So the only correct pair is trypsin and proteins, which is option (B) Column I (Enzymes): Trypsin; Column II (Component): Proteins.

rows.stem: To obtain a magnification of + 2 with a concave mirror of radius of curvature 60 cm the object distance must be
rows.solution:
For a concave mirror of radius of curvature 60 cm, \(f = -\dfrac{60}{2} = -30\) cm.

Magnification \(m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = +2\), so \(v = -2u\).

Mirror formula: \(\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}\), so \(-\dfrac{1}{2u} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{2u} = -\dfrac{1}{30}\), which gives \(u = -15\) cm.

A positive magnification means a virtual, erect image, which a concave mirror forms only when the object is between the pole and the focus; 15 cm is indeed less than 30 cm. This is option (D) \(-15\) cm.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.stem: The phenomena of light involved in the formation of rainbow are

options.label: D
options.text: Reflection, dispersion and total internal reflection.

rows.solution:
Sunlight entering a raindrop is refracted and dispersed into its colours. The light is then reflected internally at the back of the drop, and is refracted again as it comes out towards the observer. (The reflection inside the drop is not total internal reflection.)

So the phenomena are refraction, dispersion and internal reflection, which is option (C) Refraction, dispersion and internal reflection.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** An ecosystem consists of biotic components and abiotic components.

**Reason (R) :** Biotic and abiotic components play important roles for the sustenance of life and work independently in all ecosystems.
rows.context:
Q. No. 17 to 20 are Assertion – Reasoning based questions.

These consists of two statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
An ecosystem consists of all the living organisms (biotic components) of an area together with the non-living physical factors such as temperature, rainfall, wind and soil (abiotic components). So the Assertion is true.

The biotic and abiotic components do not work independently: they interact with each other, and this interaction is what sustains life in the ecosystem. So the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
A metal nitrate ‘A’ on heating gives a metal oxide along with evolution of a brown coloured gas ‘B’ and a colourless gas, which helps in burning. Aqueous solution of ‘A’ when reacted with potassium iodide forms a yellow precipitate.

(a) Identify ‘A’ and ‘B’

(b) Name the types of both the reactions involved in the above statement.
rows.solution:
(a) A is lead nitrate, \(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2}\). B, the brown gas, is nitrogen dioxide, \(\mathrm{NO_2}\). The colourless gas that helps in burning is oxygen.

\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO + 4NO_2 + O_2}\)

With potassium iodide, lead nitrate gives a yellow precipitate of lead iodide:

\(\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2 + 2KI \rightarrow PbI_2 + 2KNO_3}\)

(b) Heating lead nitrate is a (thermal) decomposition reaction. Its reaction with potassium iodide is a double displacement reaction, also called a precipitation reaction.

rows.stem: Three resistors of 6 \(\Omega\), 4 \(\Omega\) and 4 \(\Omega\) are connected together so that the total resistance is 8 \(\Omega\). Draw a diagram to show this arrangement and give reason to justify your answer.
rows.solution:
Diagram: connect the two 4 \(\Omega\) resistors in parallel with each other, and connect this pair in series with the 6 \(\Omega\) resistor.

Reason: for the parallel pair,

\(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{2}{4}\), so \(R_p = 2\,\Omega\).

The 6 \(\Omega\) resistor is in series with this combination, so the total resistance is

\(R = 6\,\Omega + 2\,\Omega = 8\,\Omega\).

rows.stem: Some plants like pea plants have tendrils which help them to climb up other plants. Explain how is it done. Name the plant hormone responsible for this movement.
rows.solution:
Tendrils are sensitive to touch. When a tendril comes in contact with a support, the part of the tendril touching the object does not grow as rapidly as the part away from it. This unequal growth makes the tendril coil around the object and cling to it, so the plant climbs up. This movement in response to touch is called thigmotropism.

The plant hormone responsible for this movement is auxin.

rows.stem: Name the phenomenon occurring in plants which are under the control of gravity, water and chemicals with one example each that shows the movement involved.
rows.solution:
Geotropism: the response to gravity. Example: roots grow downwards, in response to gravity.

Hydrotropism: the response to water. Example: roots grow towards water.

Chemotropism: the response to chemicals. Example: the growth of pollen tubes towards the ovules.

rows.stem:
A reddish brown metal used in electrical wires when powdered and heated strongly turns black. When hydrogen gas is passed over this black substance, it regains its original colour. Based on this information answer the following questions –

(a) Name the metal and the black substance formed.

(b) Write balanced chemical equations for the two reactions involved in the above information.
rows.solution:
(a) The metal is copper (Cu). The black substance is copper(II) oxide, CuO.

(b) On heating in air, copper combines with oxygen to form black copper oxide:

\(\mathrm{2Cu + O_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2CuO}\)

When hydrogen is passed over the hot copper oxide, it is reduced back to reddish brown copper:

\(\mathrm{CuO + H_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Cu + H_2O}\)

rows.stem: If a harmful chemical enters in a food chain comprising peacock, plants, rats and snakes, which of these organisms is likely to have the highest concentration of the chemical in its body. Justify your answer. Name the process involved and define it.
rows.solution:
The peacock will have the highest concentration of the chemical in its body.

The food chain is plants \(\rightarrow\) rats \(\rightarrow\) snakes \(\rightarrow\) peacock, so the peacock occupies the top trophic level. Harmful chemicals such as pesticides are not biodegradable, so they are not broken down or excreted. They accumulate at each level and their concentration increases as we move up the food chain.

The process is biomagnification: the progressive increase in the concentration of harmful, non-biodegradable chemicals at successive trophic levels of a food chain.

rows.stem:
(i) What are isomers ? Write the structures of two compounds having molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_6O}\) and give their names.

(ii) What are soaps ? How are they chemically different from detergents ? Why do soaps not work effectively in hard water ?
rows.solution:
(i) Isomers are compounds that have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae.

Two compounds with molecular formula \(\mathrm{C_3H_6O}\):

1. Propanal, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CHO}\): an aldehyde, in which the carbon at the end of the chain carries a double-bonded oxygen and a hydrogen, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2{-}C({=}O){-}H}\).

2. Propanone (acetone), \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CO{-}CH_3}\): a ketone, in which the middle carbon carries the double-bonded oxygen, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}C({=}O){-}CH_3}\).

(ii) Soaps are sodium or potassium salts of long-chain carboxylic acids, \(\mathrm{R{-}COO^-Na^+}\).

Detergents are generally sodium salts of sulphonic acids, \(\mathrm{R{-}SO_3^-Na^+}\), or ammonium salts with chloride or bromide ions. (Sodium alkyl sulphates, \(\mathrm{R{-}OSO_3^-Na^+}\), the form the marking scheme writes, are detergents too.) So a soap carries a carboxylate group, while a detergent carries a sulphonate (or sulphate) or ammonium group.

Hard water contains calcium and magnesium ions. Soap reacts with them to form an insoluble substance called scum, which sticks to the cloth, so a lot of soap is wasted and cleaning is poor. Detergents do not form insoluble salts with these ions, so they work in hard water too.

rows.stem:
(i) What is a homologous series of carbon compounds ? Write general formula for alkynes. Name and draw the electron dot structure of first homologue of this series.

(ii) State the meaning of the functional group in an organic compound. Write the formula of the functional group present in alcohols and carboxylic acids.
rows.solution:
(i) A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain. Its members have similar chemical properties, and successive members differ by a \(\mathrm{{-}CH_2{-}}\) unit.

The general formula of alkynes is \(\mathrm{C_nH_{2n-2}}\).

The first member is ethyne, \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\) (\(\mathrm{HC{\equiv}CH}\)).

Electron dot structure of ethyne: the two carbon atoms share three pairs of electrons between them (a triple bond), and each carbon shares one pair of electrons with its hydrogen atom. Each carbon then has eight electrons around it and each hydrogen two.

(ii) A functional group is an atom or a group of atoms (such as a heteroatom) bonded to the carbon chain that decides the characteristic chemical properties of the organic compound, whatever the length of the chain.

Alcohols: \(\mathrm{{-}OH}\)

Carboxylic acids: \(\mathrm{{-}COOH}\), that is \(\mathrm{{-}C({=}O){-}OH}\)
